securityControls.controlImplementationDescription: Account provisioning and deprovisioning is automated through the identity provider (Okta) with SCIM sync to MOCP; disabled accounts are removed from all systems within 1 hour via automated workflow.
Role-based access control enforces least privilege across all tenant and administrative roles; privileged access requires just-in-time elevation with automatic 8-hour expiry.
All authentication events, administrative actions, and data access to CUI are logged to the centralized SIEM with 1-year hot retention and 3-year cold storage.
All human users authenticate via phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) enforced at the identity provider; password-only authentication is disabled tenant-wide.
Network boundaries are enforced via AWS security groups and NACLs with default-deny inbound rules; a WAF inspects all inbound HTTPS traffic to the application tier.
Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 (AWS KMS-managed keys); data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher exclusively.

Baseline configurations are defined in Terraform and enforced via CI/CD for all production infrastructure; a small set of legacy batch-processing hosts are being migrated to the same pipeline, targeted for completion Q4 2026.
Authenticated vulnerability scans run weekly against all production hosts and containers; findings are tracked to remediation in the security backlog per internal SLAs.
Automated daily database snapshots are retained for 35 days and replicated cross-region; quarterly restoration tests validate recovery point and time objectives.
A managed SIEM/SOAR platform continuously correlates log sources across the environment and generates alerts routed to the 24/7 security operations rotation.

frrImplementation: This Security Decision Record is published and versioned alongside the MOCP Certification Package Overview, with metadata (schema version, publication date, package ID) embedded at the top of each machine-readable document.
frrValidation: Metadata fields are validated against the published FedRAMP JSON Schemas as part of the CI publication pipeline before any document is made public.
frrAssessment: The independent assessor confirmed all published SDR metadata fields are complete and internally consistent with the Certification Package Overview during the 2026 assessment cycle.

frrImplementation: All FedRAMP-required public information (Certification Package Overview, Trust Center contents, secure configuration guidance) is published at https://trust.meridianfed.com/mocp without authentication requirements.
frrValidation: A quarterly internal audit confirms public documentation URLs remain reachable and current.

frrImplementation: The FedRAMP ID (FR2026-MOCP-001) is included in the Certification Package Overview, the public Trust Center landing page, and the FedRAMP Marketplace listing.
A self-service Trust Center at trust.meridianfed.com/mocp hosts all certification data, ongoing certification reports, and vulnerability activity feeds for authorized agency reviewers.
frrValidation: Agency access requests are logged and reviewed monthly to confirm only authorized federal personnel have been granted access.

frrImplementation: A monitored security inbox (security@meridianfed.com) receives and routes all FedRAMP correspondence to the compliance team, with acknowledgment of receipt within one business day.
frrValidation: Inbox monitoring and routing rules are tested quarterly by sending a test message and confirming automated acknowledgment.

frrImplementation: All proposed changes are evaluated against the Adaptive/Transformative criteria during the weekly change advisory board meeting before implementation.
frrValidation: Change evaluation decisions and rationale are recorded in the change management system for audit.

frrImplementation: Vulnerability Detail Reports are generated monthly from the vulnerability management platform and published to the Trust Center per VER-RPT-VDT.
frrValidation: Report contents are cross-checked against the vulnerability scanner's raw findings export prior to publication.

frrImplementation: Accepted vulnerabilities are tracked with documented acceptance rationale and reported monthly alongside the Vulnerability Detail Report.
Vulnerability reporting occurs on a persistent monthly cadence covering all activity since the previous report, with no gaps.
Ongoing Certification Reports are published to the Trust Center quarterly, within 5 business days of the close of each reporting period.
frrValidation: Publication dates are tracked against the committed schedule in the compliance calendar.

frrImplementation: Every confirmed security incident is evaluated against FedRAMP reportability criteria within 4 hours of triage by the on-call incident commander.
frrValidation: Reportability determinations are documented in the incident ticket for later audit.

frrImplementation: All information resources within the Minimum Assessment Scope are inventoried in the asset management system, tagged by data flow and security category.
Cryptographic modules in use (AWS KMS, OpenSSL 3.x FIPS module) are documented with validation certificate references in the system security documentation.
Key Security Indicators applicable to this Certification Class are documented below with implementation, validation, and assessment statements for each.

ksiImplementation: All personnel with system access complete annual security awareness training; completion records are tracked in the HR learning management system.
ksiValidation: Training completion is reviewed quarterly against the current employee roster to identify and remediate gaps.
ksiAssessment: The independent assessor sampled 15 employee training records and confirmed 100% completion within required timeframes.
ksiTests: Quarterly training-completion reconciliation against active employee roster

ksiImplementation: All infrastructure and application changes are logged automatically through the CI/CD pipeline and AWS CloudTrail, capturing who, what, and when for every deployment.
ksiValidation: Change logs are reconciled weekly against the change advisory board's approved change list.
ksiAssessment: Assessor confirmed change logs for a sample of 20 production deployments matched approved change records with no discrepancies.

ksiImplementation: Automated integration and smoke tests run against every deployment before traffic is shifted to the new version via blue/green deployment.
ksiValidation: Deployment pipeline test results are archived and reviewed monthly for trend analysis.
ksiTests: Post-deployment smoke test suite (automated, every deploy)

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: CI pipeline run summary showing passing smoke tests

ksiImplementation: Container images are built from minimal base images with unnecessary packages and services removed; attack surface is reviewed as part of the quarterly architecture review.
ksiValidation: Automated container image scanning flags any newly introduced unnecessary packages or open ports before deployment.
ksiAssessment: Assessor reviewed a sample of container image manifests and confirmed minimal footprint.
ksiTests: Automated image scan on every container build

ksiImplementation: Network traffic between services is restricted using AWS security groups and a service mesh enforcing mutual TLS and explicit allow-listed service-to-service communication paths.
ksiValidation: Network flow logs are reviewed monthly to confirm no unexpected traffic paths have emerged.

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Security group and service mesh policy export

ksiImplementation: Access is granted strictly on a least-privilege basis via predefined IAM roles mapped to job function; no standing administrative access exists for routine operations.
ksiValidation: Quarterly access reviews confirm each user's granted permissions match their current role.
ksiAssessment: Assessor sampled 25 user accounts and confirmed permissions were consistent with least-privilege role assignments.

ksiImplementation: Elevated administrative access requires just-in-time approval through the PAM system, automatically expiring after 8 hours and requiring re-justification for renewal.
ksiValidation: PAM session logs are reviewed weekly to confirm all elevated sessions were justified and time-bound.

ksiImplementation: The incident response plan is reviewed and updated annually, and after every incident retrospective, to incorporate lessons learned.
ksiValidation: Plan revision history is tracked in version control with review sign-off from the security lead.

ksiImplementation: A managed SIEM aggregates logs from all production systems, cloud infrastructure, and identity providers, providing 24/7 correlation and alerting.
ksiValidation: SIEM alert coverage and log source health are reviewed weekly by the security operations team.
ksiAssessment: Assessor confirmed the SIEM ingests logs from all in-scope systems per the documented log source inventory.
ksiTests: Weekly SIEM log source health check

ksiImplementation: Security-relevant logs are reviewed daily by the security operations team through automated dashboards, with manual deep-dive review triggered by anomaly alerts.
ksiTests: Daily automated log review dashboard check

ksiImplementation: An automated asset inventory tool continuously discovers and catalogs all cloud resources, reconciled against the authorized boundary weekly.
ksiValidation: Inventory reconciliation reports are reviewed weekly for unauthorized or orphaned resources.

ksiImplementation: Backup frequency and retention (daily snapshots, 35-day retention, cross-region replication) are aligned with the documented recovery point objective of 24 hours.
ksiValidation: Backup completion and retention compliance are verified automatically each night with alerting on failure.
ksiAssessment: Assessor confirmed backup configuration matches the documented RPO/RTO objectives during the 2026 assessment.

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Backup job success log for June 2026

ksiImplementation: Direct software dependencies are continuously monitored for known vulnerabilities via automated software composition analysis; extension to transitive third-party service dependencies is in progress, targeted for completion Q3 2026.
ksiValidation: SCA scan results are reviewed weekly and tracked to remediation.

ksiImplementation: All application secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation every 90 days; no secrets are stored in source control or configuration files.
ksiValidation: Automated secret scanning runs on every commit to prevent accidental secret exposure.
ksiAssessment: Assessor confirmed no hardcoded secrets were found in a full repository scan.
ksiTests: Pre-commit and CI secret scanning on every push

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Secret rotation audit log for Q2 2026

ksiImplementation: Tenant data is logically isolated using per-tenant database schemas and row-level security policies, encrypted at rest with tenant-specific KMS key grants.
ksiValidation: Tenant isolation is validated through automated cross-tenant access negative testing in the CI pipeline.
ksiAssessment: Assessor's penetration test confirmed no cross-tenant data access was possible.
ksiTests: Automated cross-tenant isolation negative test suite (CI, every deploy)

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Penetration test report excerpt: tenant isolation findings
